The '''2003–04 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 102nd season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 72nd in a [[round-robin tournament]]. It contained 18 teams for the 16th and last time from the 1988–89 season. With the bottom three being relegated, the 15th placed side would face the sixth-highest team from [[Serie B]], with the winner playing in the Serie A in the subsequent [[2004–05 Serie A|2004–05]] season.

As usual, the top two teams would progress directly to the [[UEFA Champions League]] group stage, while third and fourth place would have to begin in the third qualifying round. The [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] places would be awarded to fifth and sixth place, and the winners of the [[Coppa Italia]].

[[A.C. Milan|Milan]] won their 17th ''scudetto''; [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] impressed and were pushing for the title until the last few weeks of the season; [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] only made it to the Champions League ahead of [[S.S.D. Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] and [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] on the last day thanks to [[Adriano (footballer, born February 1982)|Adriano]], who had been signed from Parma earlier in the season; Lazio won the [[Coppa Italia]] against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], handing [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] the [[UEFA Cup]] spot; [[U.S. Ancona 1905|Ancona]] were relegated with only two wins, the joint lowest tally ever ([[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]]'s 12 points in [[1994–95 Serie A]] is still the lowest ever); [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]] and [[Modena F.C.|Modena]] were also relegated; [[A.C. Perugia Calcio|Perugia]] lost their special play-off, imposed to expand the league, against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], who returned to Serie A after a two-year absence.

[[File:Andriy Shevchenko - 2004 - AC Milan (3).jpg|thumb|upright|[[AC Milan|Milan]]’s [[Andriy Shevchenko]]]]
[[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Forward (association football)|forward]] [[Andriy Shevchenko]] of [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] was the top scorer, with 24 goals. The 2003–04 league was the last professional season in the career of former [[European Footballer of the Year]] and Italian international [[Roberto Baggio]], who finished among the tournament's top ten scorers with 12 goals, and among the all-time top five scorers in Serie A, with 205 career goals. It was also the last Serie A season for Baggio's former teammate [[Giuseppe Signori]], who then moved to the [[Super League Greece]]. Signori ended his career in Italy as the seventh highest scorer ever in Serie A.

==Teams==
Eighteen teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top fourteen teams from the previous season and the four teams promoted from the [[2002–03 Serie B|Serie B]]. The promoted teams were [[AC Siena|Siena]], [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], [[US Lecce|Lecce]] and [[Ancona Calcio|Ancona]]. Sampdoria, Lecce and Ancona returned to the top flight after an absence of four, one and ten years respectively, while Siena played in the top flight for the first time in history. They replaced [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] (relegated after three seasons in the top flight), [[Piacenza Calcio|Piacenza]], [[Torino Calcio|Torino]] (both teams relegated after a two-years presence) and [[Como Calcio|Como]] (relegated after a season's presence).

==Rule changes==
Unlike [[La Liga]], which imposed a quota on the number of non-EU players on each club, Serie A clubs could sign as many non-EU players as available on domestic transfer. But for the 2003–04 season a quota was imposed on each of the clubs limiting the number of non-[[European Union|EU]], non-[[EFTA]] and non-[[Switzerland|Swiss]] players who may be signed from abroad each season,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=57329.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604164303/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=57329.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|title=Italy blocks non-EU players|date=2003-03-05|access-date=2010-03-09|publisher=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> following provisional measures<ref name=provision>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=28321.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604164248/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=28321.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|title=Italians bar non-EU imports|date=2002-07-17|access-date=2010-03-09|publisher=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> introduced in the [[2002–03 Serie A|2002–03 season]], which allowed Serie A & B clubs to sign only one non-EU player in the 2002 summer transfer window.
